intro.lead1: This is the documentation of version 1 of the EasyConvert API, the paths under /api/v1. Send a file and a target format, and get the converted file back.
intro.lead2: This page covers the base URL, authentication, errors and limits. The menu lists the endpoints. To send a first request, follow the <quickstart>Quickstart</quickstart>.
intro.lead3: Every endpoint is also described in the <openapi>OpenAPI document</openapi> (JSON), which an API client or a code generator can read.
intro.baseUrl: The base URL of the API is {origin}. Every path in this documentation starts there, for example {origin}/api/v1/convert.
intro.authentication: A request carries an API key. The few endpoints that need none say so on their page.
intro.apiKeys1: Sign in and create a key on the API keys page of the dashboard. A key starts with ec_live_ and is shown once, when it is created.
intro.apiKeys2: Send the key in the x-api-key header, or as a bearer token in the Authorization header:
intro.apiKeys3: A key can be limited to IP addresses or CIDR ranges and can expire. A request from another address, or with an expired or revoked key, is refused.
intro.scopes: A key holds one or more scopes. Each endpoint names the scope it needs, and a key without it is answered 403.

scopeAllows.convert:write: Convert files, upload files, and create and cancel jobs.
scopeAllows.convert:read: Show and list jobs, read the OCR languages and the offset of an upload.
scopeAllows.storage:download: Download the results of conversions made with the key.

intro.errors1: A refused or failed request is answered with a status of 400 or more and a problem details body (RFC 9457) of type application/problem+json:

problemFields.type: A URI reference identifying the problem type.
problemFields.title: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.
problemFields.status: The HTTP status code generated for this occurrence.
problemFields.detail: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.
problemFields.instance: A URI reference identifying the specific occurrence.
problemFields.invalidParams: List of invalid parameters for validation failures.
problemFields.code: The cause of a refusal of a conversion, stable across releases, when the error that decided the answer names one (for example `engine_unavailable`).
problemFields.error: Legacy compatibility error message mirroring detail.

intro.errors2: The type names the cause, and some causes add fields of their own, such as dailyLimit and remaining for a used-up allowance. A few routes, Downloads and Usage, answer JSON with success set to false and an error sentence instead. The statuses mean:

statuses.400: The request is malformed: a missing field, an unknown format or a conversion between two formats that is not offered.
statuses.401: No API key, or a key that is unknown, expired or revoked.
statuses.403: The key lacks the scope, or the request comes from an address the key does not allow.
statuses.404: The job, upload or file does not exist, or belongs to another account.
statuses.409: A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running, or the job cannot be cancelled any more.
statuses.413: The file or the request is over a limit; the detail names the limit.
statuses.415: The body is not of the type the endpoint takes.
statuses.422: The request is well formed but cannot be done: a protected document, a file whose content does not match its format, or an Idempotency-Key reused with another request.
statuses.429: The daily allowance is used up, the key exceeded its request rate, or too many conversions are running. See Retry-After.
statuses.500: The conversion failed on the server. Nothing is charged.
statuses.503: The conversion needs an engine this server does not have.
statuses.504: The conversion ran past its time limit. Send it as a job instead.

intro.limits: The daily allowance and the conversions at once count for the account, whichever key it uses; the request rate counts for each key.
intro.dailyAllowance1: An account on the free plan runs {daily} conversions a day on the server; the count starts again at midnight UTC. Only a conversion that finishes counts: a refused, failed or cancelled conversion is not charged.
intro.dailyAllowance2: Each conversion answer carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (the seconds until the count starts again). When none is left, a conversion is answered 429 with Retry-After. The Usage endpoint reads the same numbers.
intro.requestRate: A key on the free plan sends up to {burst} requests at once and {perSecond} a second after that. A request over that rate is answered 429 with Retry-After.
intro.concurrentConversions: An account on the free plan has up to {concurrent} conversions queued or running at once. Another one is answered 429 with Retry-After and takes nothing from the allowance.
intro.fileSize1: One request carries at most {requestMax} of file and form fields. A file up to {fileMax} is uploaded in parts through <uploads>Uploads</uploads> and converted by a <jobs>job</jobs>.
intro.fileSize2: POST /api/v1/convert converts a file of up to {syncMax} while the request waits; a larger file is queued as a job and answered 202.

quickstart.lead: This guide sends a file to the API and saves the converted file, first in one request and then through an upload and a job. The commands use curl and read the key from the EASYCONVERT_API_KEY environment variable.
quickstart.createKey1: Sign in and open the API keys page of the dashboard. Create a key with the convert:write, convert:read and storage:download scopes.
quickstart.createKey2: Copy the key when it is shown; it is shown only once. Keep it on the server and never put it in a web page or an app.
quickstart.convert1: Send the file and the target format as a form to POST /api/v1/convert. With Accept: application/octet-stream the answer is the converted file:
quickstart.convert2: Without that header the answer is JSON with the name, size and downloadUrl of the result. See Downloads.
quickstart.convert3: A file over {syncMax} is not converted while the request waits: it is queued as a job and the answer is 202 with the jobId and its statusUrl. Continue with the job as below.
quickstart.large1: One request carries at most {requestMax}. A larger file is uploaded in parts and then converted by a job:
quickstart.largeStep1: Start a direct upload. The answer lists an upload URL for each part.
quickstart.largeStep2: Send each part with PUT to its URL and keep the ETag of each answer.
quickstart.largeStep3: Complete the upload with the part numbers and their entity tags. The answer holds the storageKey of the file.
quickstart.large2: Create a job for the stored file:
quickstart.large3: The answer is 202 with the jobId. Ask for the job until its status is completed or failed; a finished job names its file in result.downloadUrl. A webhookUrl sent with the job is told instead, so nothing needs to ask.
quickstart.download1: Download the result from its downloadUrl with the key:
quickstart.download2: A result is deleted shortly after it has been downloaded completely, and after a while when nobody downloads it, so save it when it is ready.

access.public: None. Anyone can call this endpoint.
access.key: An API key in the x-api-key or Authorization header.
access.keyScoped: An API key with the {scopes} scope, in the x-api-key or Authorization header.
access.optionalKey: An API key, or none for a file whose URL is all its access.
access.optionalKeyScoped: An API key with the {scopes} scope for a file of an account. A file made without an account needs none: its URL is all its access.

convert-a-file.title: Convert a file
convert-a-file.lead: Converts one file while the request waits. Send the file and the target format as a form. With Accept: application/octet-stream the answer is the converted file; without it, JSON that names the result. A large file is queued as a job instead, as the 202 answer below says.

create-a-job.title: Create a job
create-a-job.lead: Queues a conversion and answers at once with the id of the job, while the conversion runs on its own. Use it for a file sent through Uploads (by its storageKey) and for a conversion that takes longer than a request can wait. With webhookUrl the job sends job.completed or job.failed there when it ends.

show-a-job.title: Show a job
show-a-job.lead: Answers with the status and progress of a job, and its result once it is completed.

list-jobs.title: List jobs
list-jobs.lead: Lists the jobs of the account, optionally only those in the given states.

cancel-a-job.title: Cancel a job
cancel-a-job.lead: Stops a job that is waiting or running. A cancelled job is not charged.

start-a-direct-upload.title: Start a direct upload
start-a-direct-upload.lead: Starts an upload in parts and answers with an upload URL for each part. The URLs are valid for 15 minutes.

upload-a-part.title: Upload a part
upload-a-part.lead: Sends one part to its upload URL. The URL carries its own signature, so the request sends no key.

complete-a-direct-upload.title: Complete a direct upload
complete-a-direct-upload.lead: Joins the parts into one file and checks that its content matches its format. The answer holds the storageKey a job converts.

abort-a-direct-upload.title: Abort a direct upload
abort-a-direct-upload.lead: Stops an upload and deletes the parts sent so far.

create-a-resumable-upload.title: Create a resumable upload
create-a-resumable-upload.lead: Starts an upload by the tus 1.0.0 protocol, which can resume after a broken connection. A tus client library sends these requests for you.

append-a-chunk.title: Append a chunk
append-a-chunk.lead: Adds bytes to a resumable upload at the offset the server holds.

read-the-upload-offset.title: Read the upload offset
read-the-upload-offset.lead: Answers with how many bytes the server has received, so an interrupted upload can resume there.

terminate-a-resumable-upload.title: Terminate a resumable upload
terminate-a-resumable-upload.lead: Stops a resumable upload and deletes what it received.

discover-the-upload-capabilities.title: Discover the upload capabilities
discover-the-upload-capabilities.lead: Answers with the tus version, extensions and largest size the server takes, in the response headers.

download-a-file.title: Download a file
download-a-file.lead: Downloads a result by the key in its downloadUrl. One byte range can be asked for, so a broken download can continue.

list-formats.title: List formats
list-formats.lead: Lists every format with its category and the formats it converts to.

list-ocr-languages.title: List OCR languages
list-ocr-languages.lead: Lists the languages text recognition knows, and whether this server has the data for each. Name one in the ocrLanguage option by its code.

inspect-an-archive.title: Inspect an archive
inspect-an-archive.lead: Lists the entries of an archive with their sizes and whether they are encrypted, without unpacking it.

show-the-daily-allowance.title: Show the daily allowance
show-the-daily-allowance.lead: Answers with the conversions the account has run today, how many are left and when the count starts again.

pdf.desc: PDF is an open ISO standard format for electronic document exchange. It encapsulates formatted text, vector graphics, raster images, and embedded fonts independent of operating system or viewer hardware.

docx.desc: DOCX is an XML-based document container used by Microsoft Word. It packages formatted text, tables, charts, embedded media, and styles inside a compressed ZIP archive.

doc.desc: DOC is a binary document format developed by Microsoft for Word 97 through 2003. It stores styled text, inline graphics, tables, and formatting inside an OLE compound file container.

csv.desc: CSV stores two-dimensional tabular records as plain UTF-8 text lines with delimiter-separated fields and RFC 4180 quoting rules.

json.desc: JSON is a text data-interchange format encoding key-value objects, arrays, numbers, booleans, and UTF-8 strings per RFC 8259 and ECMA-404.

xlsx.desc: XLSX packages multi-sheet workbooks, typed cell values, shared string tables, formulas, and number formats inside a ZIP-compressed OpenXML archive.

xls.desc: XLS is the BIFF8 binary workbook format used by Excel 97 through 2003, storing worksheets, cell records, and formulas in a Compound File Binary stream.

pptx.desc: PPTX stores presentation slides, master layouts, DrawingML vector shapes, embedded images, and speaker notes inside an OpenXML ZIP package.

mp4.desc: MP4 is a digital multimedia container used to store video, audio, and subtitle streams. Derived from the ISO Base Media File Format, it combines high compression efficiency with native browser and hardware playback.

mp3.desc: MP3 is a lossy compressed audio format, readable by almost every player and device.

wav.desc: WAV is an uncompressed audio container storing linear pulse-code modulation (LPCM) samples. It records acoustic waveforms sample-for-sample without lossy compression artifacts.

aac.desc: AAC is a lossy audio format designed as the successor to MP3, common in MP4 and M4A files.

flac.desc: FLAC is an open, royalty-free lossless audio codec. Compressed FLAC streams decode back to an exact bit-for-bit match of the source PCM audio.

ogg.desc: OGG is an open multimedia bitstream container commonly paired with the Vorbis or Opus audio codecs for patent-free streaming and game asset delivery.

m4a.desc: M4A is an audio-only MPEG-4 container carrying AAC or Apple Lossless (ALAC) streams alongside structured chapter and cover-art metadata.

png.desc: PNG is a raster graphics file format using lossless DEFLATE compression. It supports indexed palettes, greyscale, and full RGBA alpha transparency up to 16 bits per channel.

jpg.desc: JPG is the ISO standard for continuous-tone photographic images, applying Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) compression tuned for natural colour gradients.

jpeg.desc: JPEG is the standard continuous-tone photographic format identical in bitstream structure to JPG, using DCT block compression for natural imagery.

webp.desc: WebP provides both lossy VP8 intra-frame coding and lossless dictionary compression for web imagery, supporting alpha transparency, ICC profiles, and animation.

avif.desc: AVIF stores AV1 intra-coded still images inside an ISO HEIF container, supporting 8-bit, 10-bit, and 12-bit colour depths alongside HDR transfer functions.

heic.desc: HEIC stores HEVC (H.265) intra-coded photographs inside an ISO Base Media container, cutting storage size roughly in half relative to baseline JPEG.

svg.desc: SVG is an XML vector graphics specification describing two-dimensional paths, shapes, text, and gradients mathematically so artwork renders sharply at any DPI.

gif.desc: GIF is an indexed-palette bitmap format using lossless LZW compression for up to 256 colours per frame and looping frame sequences.

epub.desc: EPUB packages XHTML content documents, CSS stylesheets, fonts, and navigation manifests in a ZIP container for reflowable digital books.

mobi.desc: MOBI is a binary PalmDOC-derived e-book container developed by Mobipocket for portable e-ink readers, bundling HTML markup, images, and chapter offsets.

zip.desc: ZIP bundles one or more files and directory trees with independent per-entry DEFLATE compression and a central directory index.

rar.desc: RAR is a compressed archive container supporting solid dictionary compression, Reed-Solomon recovery records, and multi-volume split archives.

7z.desc: 7Z is an open modular archive container using LZMA and LZMA2 dictionary compression with large solid blocks and optional AES-256 encryption.

tar.desc: TAR serializes files and directory hierarchies sequentially in 512-byte blocks while preserving POSIX permissions, ownership, and modification timestamps.

dxf.desc: DXF is a tagged CAD data exchange format representing 2D and 3D entities, layers, blocks, arcs, polylines, and splines for CAD/CAM interoperability.

ttf.desc: TTF defines quadratic Bézier glyph outlines, character-to-glyph cmap tables, kerning metrics, and hinting instructions in a single binary font file.

woff2.desc: WOFF2 wraps TrueType or OpenType glyph tables with font-specific preprocessing and Brotli compression for `@font-face` delivery on the web.

security.heading: Security & Data Handling
security.intro: Built around isolated execution and short-lived storage boundaries.

tls.heading: TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption
tls.body: Uploads, signed storage transfers, and result downloads run strictly over encrypted HTTPS channels.

sandbox.heading: Sandboxed Browser & Worker Execution
sandbox.body: Some conversions run in your browser; the others run in isolated workers on our servers.

cleanup.heading: Automatic File Cleanup
cleanup.body: An uploaded file is deleted 10 minutes after the last job that reads it ends. A converted file is deleted 10 minutes after you download it, or an hour after conversion if you never do.

api.heading: REST API & Batch Workflows
api.intro: Automate single-file conversions via POST /api/v1/convert or submit multi-step DAG pipelines to POST /api/v1/jobs with signed webhook delivery.

quality.heading: High-Quality Conversions
quality.intro: We compare our output with established tools every night.

measured.heading: Measured against reference tools
measured.body: Every night we convert the same test files with our converters and with established ones, and compare quality and speed.

options.heading: Settings that fit the format
options.body: The options change with the file you choose, such as image quality, audio bitrate or video resolution.

formats.heading: Hundreds of formats
formats.body: {formats} formats in {categories} categories, from everyday documents and photos to camera RAW, CAD drawings and fonts.

purpose.heading: Purpose-Built File Conversion Utility
purpose.body: EasyConvert converts files across {count} registered formats spanning documents, spreadsheets, presentations, raster and RAW images, vector graphics, CAD drawings, audio, video, fonts, ebooks, and archives.

architecture.heading: Browser and Server Conversion
architecture.body: Some formats run on your device through WebAssembly and WebCodecs. The others run in isolated workers on our servers, reached over TLS 1.3. A converted file is deleted 10 minutes after you download it, or an hour after conversion if you never do.

transport.heading: TLS 1.3 Transport Encryption
transport.body: All HTTPS traffic uses TLS 1.3 with strict HSTS headers, CSRF validation on cookie-authenticated routes, and scoped bearer keys for programmatic API calls across {count} supported formats.

isolation.heading: Sandboxed Browser & Worker Isolation
isolation.body: Browser conversions stay inside the browser's origin sandbox. Server conversions run in resource-limited worker processes with strict input validation, archive decompression limits, and automatic deletion of output files.

conformance.heading: Conformance Target
conformance.body: EasyConvert targets Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA conformance across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports in both light and dark themes.

keyboard.heading: Keyboard Navigation & Shortcuts
keyboard.body: Every interactive control is operable with a keyboard alone. A skip link jumps directly to #main-content, focus indicators remain visible on all interactive elements, format selectors and tabs support arrow and tab key navigation, and modal dialogs use native HTML '<'dialog> focus containment with Escape dismissal.

landmarks.heading: Screen Reader Landmarks & Live Announcements
landmarks.body: Pages expose semantic '<'header>, '<'nav>, '<'main>, and '<'footer> landmarks, sequential heading levels from h1 through h3, explicit '<'label htmlFor> associations on every text input and selector, descriptive aria-label names on icon-only controls, and polite status regions for conversion progress and clipboard confirmation.

contrast.heading: Visual Contrast, Motion & Zoom
contrast.body: Text keeps at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio and the borders of text fields keep at least 3:1 across light and dark palettes, and buttons are identified by their labels rather than by their outlines. Form controls use a minimum 16px text size to prevent forced viewport zoom on mobile browsers, primary and icon buttons provide 44px touch targets, layouts reflow cleanly at 390px width and 200% browser zoom without horizontal page scroll, and non-essential motion honours prefers-reduced-motion.

feedback.heading: Feedback & Assistance
feedback.body: If you encounter an accessibility barrier on any EasyConvert page or API tool, contact our team so we can reproduce and resolve the issue.

daily.question: How many conversions can I run?
daily.answer: {anonymous, plural, one {# conversion} other {# conversions}} a day without an account and {daily, plural, one {# conversion} other {# conversions}} a day with a free account. The count starts again every day at midnight UTC. Conversions that run in your browser use none of our servers and are not counted.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. You can convert files without signing in. An account gives you the dashboard and API keys.

limits.question: What other limits apply?
limits.answer: A file can be up to {fileSize}. You can run {concurrent} conversions at the same time, and one conversion can run for up to {processing, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.

deletion.question: When are my files deleted?
deletion.answer: A converted file is deleted {deletion, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} after you download it, or an hour after the conversion if you never download it. An uploaded file is deleted {deletion, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} after the last job that reads it ends.

api.question: Can I use the API for free?
api.answer: Yes. Create an API key in your account and send requests to it. API requests count against the same {daily, plural, one {# conversion} other {# conversions}} a day.

paid.question: Can I buy a paid plan?
paid.answer: Paid plans are marked "Coming soon" until they go on sale. When they do, you subscribe on this page, and you manage or cancel the subscription from your dashboard.

cta.body: Convert up to {anonymous, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} a day, no account and no credit card needed.
